extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate/early-graduate math students, math enthusiasts, and potential contributors to the Napkin project
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and project description for The Napkin, a light, mostly self-contained introduction to higher mathematics (roughly undergraduate to first-year graduate level) that emphasizes bird's-eye views and intuition over full textbook-style detail. Also describes contribution workflow and project status for collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and intended level
rubrics_metrics.description: An Infinitely Large Napkin is a light and mostly self-contained introduction to higher math, roughly ranging from the undergraduate syllabus to first-year graduate topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides general bird’s-eye views of main ideas of fields and what makes them interesting; not intended to be as detailed as a full textbook but covers a wide range of topics (see listed parts/chapters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of detail and precision
rubrics_metrics.description: The Napkin is less detailed than a real textbook (but more precise than pop-math books).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions and theorem statements will typically be complete and precise, but explanations for why a result 'should' be true will supersede formal proofs; expect intuition/heuristics rather than exhaustive formal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumed background
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers are expected to be familiar with writing/reading proofs; the Napkin is not aimed at absolute beginners who lack proof exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical approach (bird's-eye/intuition-first)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize bird’s-eye views and what makes areas interesting; explanations and intuition are prioritized over full formal proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use intuition and high-level explanations to convey why results are true; provide precise statements and definitions while deferring many formal proofs in favor of heuristic understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems and solutions availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts include problems and solutions, though many chapters still lack problems or solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The project aims to include problems/solutions for parts, but completeness varies; community solutions repositories (human-readable and Lean4) are available and encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred method for submitting corrections, suggestions, or comments is via pull requests on GitHub; use issues for longer discussion or general action items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author highly appreciates corrections/suggestions; submit a PR for direct fixes and an issue when a broader conversation or planning is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project versioning convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The project follows semantic versioning (semver); version number 1.6 indicates the addition of a few new chapters and many typo fixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Version numbers communicate scope of changes (e.g., additions vs. fixes); check the repository for revision history and the most recent compiled draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and distribution constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: PDFs for individual parts are available, and a full PDF can be downloaded; note that hyperlinks that span across parts will not work in per-part PDFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If figures are needed, consult the all-generated-files folder; an auto-generated text table of contents and a flowchart by chapter number are provided to help navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community formalization and tooling
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a community working on both human-readable and Lean4 proofs of Napkin problems and examples (repositories for napkin-community/proofs and napkin-community/solutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community contributions include human-readable solutions written in Typst and formal Lean4 proofs; rendered human-readable solutions are available at the project's GitHub Pages site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project completeness/status transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Several chapters are scheduled but not yet written, and many chapters still lack problems or solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site explicitly notes which parts are TODO; readers/contributors should expect work-in-progress content and refer to the source repository for the most recent state.
